pf.license.need: always: each optometrist holds their own active license from the state's optometry board
pf.license.who: each person; opticians only where the state licenses them (a switch from the state form); the practice too where the state's form registers eye care offices or their owners
pf.license.ask: each optometrist's license number in their invite reply (or the owner sends it); an optician's license number where the state asks; the practice's registration from the owner
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.scope: what an optometrist may treat, and which eye drops and medicines they may use, comes from the state form (a switch); a visit the license doesn't cover is never offered
pf.license.away: eye exams at a care home, a school or a home only where the state's rules allow them; any registration for exams away from the office, from the state form (a switch)
pf.license.eyewear: glasses and contact lenses are sold only from a valid prescription; any optician's license or dispensing rule comes from the state form (a switch)
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking; every company in Rosie's chain signs one with Rosie
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form asks for it

pf.services.shape: visit types in an exam room, each with a set length; an exam has two parts (the optician's pre-tests, then the eye doctor's exam); glasses and contacts are ordered after the exam and picked up, or delivered, when they're ready; every visit needs a free exam room
pf.services.examples: the example offices' own prices (Lee Eye Care and Lee Eye Visits), not a standard; a plan pays its own in-network amount, and the patient's share is an estimate

list.after: the patient's share at the front desk

list.name: Contact lens fitting (added to an eye exam)
list.note: many vision plans don't pay it; a new lens gets a trial pair first, and the contacts prescription comes once the fit is final

list.note: any extra test is priced and OK'd before it's done

list.after: at the front desk, or billed to the plan
list.note: a parent or guardian books, signs the consent and stays (or signs the school's consent form)

list.name: Contact lens follow-up
list.length: 15 min, 1 to 2 weeks after the fitting
list.note: booked at checkout by the staff

list.name: Glasses (frame and lenses)

list.before: not booked: ordered at the visit

list.name: Contact lens supply
list.kind: ordered after the fitting is final
list.before: not booked: ordered at the desk
list.after: paid at the front desk when ordered

list.name: School vision day
list.price: set with the school: free to families, or billed to each child's plan

pf.services.capacity: one patient per exam room; the portable eye exam kit is booked like a person
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the patient is always there
pf.services.online: none: the example offices don't do eye exams by video, since an exam needs the office's own equipment

beforeTimes: for you, your child, or someone you help (a care home resident)
which visit: an eye exam, a contact lens fitting too, or an eye problem visit (the office's own visit types; never a symptom typed into the AI)
a vision plan or medical insurance (its name only), or paying yourself
afterTime: anything the office should know to help, like a wheelchair or needing an interpreter
for a care home or school visit: the place's name, the room, and who meets the eye doctor
securePage: plan member ID, the plan holder and a photo of the card (the vision plan, or the medical insurance for an eye problem)
health history: medicines, allergies, eye conditions, diabetes
current glasses and contact lens details (the brand and power from the box), and the last eye exam date
a parent's or guardian's consent for anyone under 18, or the consent of the person who decides for an adult who can't
pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; the care home's staff for a resident, with the decider's consent on the secure page; a minor alone only where the state's rules let minors consent to eye care (a switch)
pf.questions.neverAsked: Rosie never asks for symptoms, reasons, results or prescriptions in the AI chat; what a patient types anyway is checked for danger, and the details go only to the secure page

stop.words: sudden vision loss, sudden flashes of light, or a shadow or curtain across the vision
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911. Don't wait for an eye visit.
stop.booking: no booking; the same words are repeated if a same-day request is declined, and if it starts before a booked visit (the visit stays booked and the owner is told)

stop.words: a chemical splash in the eye, or something stuck in it
stop.say: Rinse a chemical splash with clean running water right away, and call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 or 911. Don't rub something stuck in the eye: go to the emergency room or call 911.
stop.booking: no booking; the words are fixed and the same for everyone

stop.words: an eye hit hard or cut, or sudden bad eye pain with a headache or throwing up
stop.say: This needs care now. Go to the nearest emergency room or call 911.

goOn.words: red, itchy, sore or dry eyes with nothing else
goOn.what: matched to the office's own eye problem visit; Rosie never judges how urgent it is, and same-day times need the owner's OK

pf.safety.always: the general screen: danger to life, fire, gas or a medical emergency gets 911, and words about self-harm get 988

steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before the visit (a same-day visit: before the time is held); one reminder before it's due
steps.who: every new patient; returning patients once a year, or when their health changes
steps.result: not done by its due date: Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page at the desk or the door, before any pre-test), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the front desk, by hand
steps.who: every patient who names a plan
steps.result: covered; some services only (like a contact lens fitting the plan won't pay); not covered; or can't check now (the desk checks later, and the patient may cancel free); the plan's exam not due yet: keep the time at the office's own price, or move it to the date the plan allows

steps.name: A written price estimate for self-pay patients

steps.result: a to-do for the front desk, with its due date

steps.name: The care home's or school's OK

pf.first_steps.prep: bring your glasses, your contact lens box or its prescription, a photo ID and the plan card; the eyes may be dilated and stay blurry and light-sensitive for a few hours, so bring sunglasses and plan a ride home; at a care home: the medicine list ready with the nurse

pf.visit.checkIn: at the office: the check-in code at the front desk; at a care home or school: the code from the patient, or from the nurse or staff member named on the booking
pf.visit.parts: the optician's pre-tests first (vision, eye pressure, the current glasses or contacts measured, a retina photo if chosen), then the eye doctor's exam
pf.visit.beforeWork: the optician reads the health history and asks about changes before any test
pf.visit.dilation: only the eye doctor decides on dilating drops; they take about 20 minutes to work, and the eyes stay blurry for a few hours, so a ride home is suggested; a retina photo can sometimes be used instead
pf.visit.contacts: a new contact lens gets a trial pair and a short follow-up, included in the fitting; the contacts prescription is given once the fit is final
pf.visit.prescriptions: the glasses prescription is given right after the exam, with no extra fee and without asking, and the contacts prescription once the fit is final, where the rules require it; the patient signs a receipt where the rules ask; buying glasses or contacts here is never required; prescriptions never go through Rosie
pf.visit.changes: an extra test, like a retina photo, is priced and OK'd before it's done; a medical problem found at a routine exam may move the visit to the medical plan, with the share shown first
pf.visit.orders: glasses are ordered at the visit and ready in about 7 to 10 days; the staff texts READY when they're in (or LATE with a new date), and the frame is fitted at pick-up, or delivered and fitted at a care home; not picked up in 2 weeks: one call, then one last text; paid orders are kept, with no storage fee
pf.visit.done: the check-in code or DONE; the eye doctor's notes, results and prescriptions stay in the office's own records, never in Rosie or a text
pf.visit.away: a portable eye exam kit; the care home's nurse is told when the visit is done

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking for any eye visit, and no card saved (the example offices bill vision and medical plans, and charge no fees); at a care home: nothing taken when a plan pays, and private pay gets the bill Rosie texts after; new glasses delivered at a care home: a $40 deposit when booked
pf.money.plans: vision plans for routine exams and glasses (an exam every 12 months, a frame allowance, a lens copay; a contact lens fitting is often not covered); medical insurance for an eye problem visit; the office's own list of plans it takes; the front desk checks each plan by hand and records it; the patient's share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.glasses: the plan's frame allowance and lens copay come off; the example office takes half the patient's share as a deposit at the front desk when ordering, and the rest at pick-up
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay patient is told while booking that they can get a written price estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.fees: none at the example offices: no late-cancel or missed-visit fee; a switch lets an office turn one on, with a card saved for it and the same fee for every patient who may be charged one
pf.money.feeFree: a switch: no fee ever for patients whose plan or the state's rules bar one (like Medicaid, where that applies), or whom the owner marks fee-free
pf.money.after: claims sent by the office; the patient pays their share at the front desk, its own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the office, not by Rosie's text; at a care home, the office bills its own way, and private pay gets the bill Rosie texts
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.caps: deposit cap: from the state form; fee limits for plan patients: from the plan's and the state's rules
pf.money.tax: no tax line on exams; any sales tax on glasses or contact lenses comes from the state form (a switch)

pf.messages.never: texts carry only the practice's name, the date, the time, the address and a secure link: never the visit type, the plan, the reason, results or a prescription; at the office, not the eye doctor's name either; when the eye doctor or optician comes to a care home, school or home, their name stays, for the door check; a READY text says only that the order is ready to pick up
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the patient's initials only (A.M., never Alex M.)
pf.messages.minors: a minor's texts go to the parent or guardian; a minor who may consent alone gets texts only on their own phone, with no visit type
pf.messages.decider: for an adult who can't consent, the texts go to the person who decides, and the code to whoever meets the eye doctor

pf.staff.licenses: each optometrist's own license, per state; opticians only where the state licenses them
pf.staff.skills: eye doctors: exams, contact lens fittings, dilating drops, eye problem visits and prescriptions; opticians: pre-tests, frames and lenses, glasses fittings and repairs, and teaching contact lens care; only people cleared for visits away go to care homes and schools
pf.staff.supervision: an optician's pre-tests are read by the eye doctor; which tests an optician may run comes from the state form (a switch)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs same-day eye problem visits, and anything an optician flags
pf.staff.standIn: an eye doctor out: another eye doctor takes the exam, or new times; an optician out: the eye doctor runs the pre-tests, and the glasses desk waits; a one-doctor day means new times for that day's patients
pf.staff.away: the team at a care home or school is the people cleared for visits away, with the portable eye exam kit

pf.rules.prescriptions: the glasses prescription after every exam, with no extra fee and without asking, and the contacts prescription once the fit is final; a contacts prescription lasts at least as long as the rules set, unless the eye doctor records a medical reason; booking never depends on buying glasses or contacts here, and a patient may buy them anywhere (each where the rules require it, a switch)
pf.rules.receipt: a signed receipt for a prescription, where the rules ask: a secure form at the visit (A8-52, B8-55)
pf.rules.records: eye records are kept by the office for as long as the state's rules require (a child's records may be kept longer); a delete request removes only Rosie's own booking details, never the office's records
pf.rules.copies: a patient's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the office, and on a visit away from it
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a minor, and at what age a minor may consent alone (a switch from the state form)
pf.rules.host: a visit at a care home or school only under the host's written OK, and the host's sign-in rules; visit days at a host's place (S1-58) need the host's standing OK on file; the example's care home visits are booked one resident at a time under the care home's OK, so no visit days are set
pf.rules.ads: no free-exam or price claims the state's rules don't allow
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form

pf.edges.lateArrival: more than 15 minutes late: still seen, but the contact lens part may move to another visit (the office decides; Rosie never changes the booking itself)
pf.edges.noRide: a patient with no ride home after dilating drops: the eye doctor may use a retina photo instead, or the patient waits until the drops wear off; Rosie only puts the ride note in the reminder
pf.edges.standIn: an eye doctor out: a stand-in eye doctor, or new times with no fee
pf.edges.forms: a form not done by its due date: one reminder, then Sam keeps the visit (signed on the secure page before any pre-test), moves it, or cancels with no fee (A7-74, B7-61)
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.planNotDue: the plan's exam isn't due yet (one every 12 months): keep the time at the office's own price, or move it to the date the plan allows
pf.edges.glassesLate: the lab is late: the staff texts LATE with a new date, and the patient hears before the old date passes
pf.edges.notPickedUp: glasses not picked up in 2 weeks: one call, then one last text; paid orders are kept, with no storage fee
pf.edges.contactsElsewhere: a question about buying contacts elsewhere goes to the office; once the prescription is given, the patient may buy them anywhere
pf.edges.twoBookings: a patient with a contact lens follow-up and an eye exam both open: Rosie asks which one before any change
pf.edges.healthQuestion: a question about medicine or eye drops before the visit goes to the eye doctor; Rosie gives no advice
pf.edges.careHome: the resident is out (at the hospital, or asleep): the nurse says so, and the visit moves with no fee
pf.edges.urgent: no service is sent now and nobody is on call (S2-30, S2-31): an eye problem gets the soonest same-day time, with the owner's OK; vision loss, flashes or a curtain over the vision get the 911 words
pf.edges.other: all other edge cases the generic way

notes:
From: the dentist pilot (work/prof/dentist.json, current). Why: eye care runs like a dental clinic: new-patient forms and health details only on the secure page, a vision or medical plan checked by hand at the desk, the share paid at the front desk, no Rosie $2 for a health practice, and a mobile side at care homes and schools. Its renames, no-$2 pairs, off ops and private-text words were carried over and turned into eye care words (subs.js), then reworked.
Names: Sam Lee, an eye doctor (optometrist), owns Lee Eye Visits LLC (the master's main company: mobile eye care and eyewear, 75 Market St) and Lee Eye Care LLC (the second company: the office, 355 Aspen Ave). Flow A is at the office; flow B at Sunrise Gardens care home, 48 Linden Rd, Room 12, where Alex lives.
People: Riley and Avery became Elena (eye doctor) and Clara (optician) at the office; Jordan and Casey became Marcus (eye doctor, who also does eyewear) and Leo (optician) on the mobile team. Sam is an eye doctor too, so he is the stand-in for an exam: an optician never stands in for the eye doctor (A7-15 to A7-21, B7-19 to B7-22, S11-46, S11-80). Grace stays the master's form example customer.
Kinds of work: plumbing became mobile eye care, electrical became eyewear (it waits for Marcus's license and the company's registration), the barbershop became the eye care office. Licenses are each optometrist's own; opticians, the office's registration and any registration for exams away from an office are switches from the state form.
Prices are the example offices' own, not a standard. The office: eye exam $120 (the master's own clinic example, A4-58), contact lens fitting $45 (the master's A4-57 'lens fitting', used as the main story), eye problem visit $140, glasses check $40, retina photo $20, child's eye exam $120. Glasses: a $189 frame, the plan's $150 allowance and a $25 lens copay, so Alex's share is $64, half as a deposit at the desk. Mobile: eye exam at a care home $179, eye problem visit from an $89 eye check ($245 in all at the visit), new glasses delivered and fitted $150 with a $40 deposit, low vision aids from a quote ($640).
Money A: list|none|counter only. Every office visit takes nothing at booking and saves no card (the old flowchart: no deposits, no missed-visit fees); the desk checks the plan and takes the share at the front desk. The glasses deposit and the rest at pick-up are paid at the counter too, so they ride on the same path (A9-18, A10-22, A10-x01), not a deposit at booking. Left out: a card saved, a hold, a deposit or full price at booking, Rosfield's bill and the saved card (the office has a front desk and charges no fees), photos (nothing is priced from photos) and quoted-at-the-visit (an eye problem visit has a list price; an extra test is priced first at A8-33).
Money B: list|none|own is the main path (an eye exam billed to the resident's plan the office's own way); list|none|bill is the same exam paid privately (Rosie texts the $179 bill at DONE); visit|none|own is an eye problem at the care home (only the $89 eye check promised, the rest OK'd at the visit); list|deposit|bill is new glasses delivered and fitted from a past exam's prescription ($40 deposit on the secure page, the $110 rest on Rosfield's bill). Left out: holds, a saved card, full price at booking and photos.
No fees: the example offices charge no late-cancel or missed-visit fee, so S11-22's 'Yes: the fee they agreed to' is off in both flows and every patient is fee-free (S11-35, S11-36). Where a deposit was paid (new glasses), a late cancel or a missed visit keeps nothing: B7-10, B7-14, B8-16, B8-60 and B8-66 say the $40 stays for a new time or is refunded.
No $2: eye care is a health practice, so the pilot's no-$2 pairs and the master's no-$2 branches (S1-62, S1-65, S11-92, S11-94 off on the $2 side) stay; S11-92's line now says neither business pays it.
Sign-up now says how eye care is really paid (S1-12 to S1-18, S1-38 to S1-51): nothing taken before an exam, a plan billed the office's own way, private pay by Rosfield's bill, a $40 deposit only for new glasses, no tips and no fees. S1-47's color-quote rule became 'same-day visits need Sam's OK', and S11-08 (a photo quote for Sam's OK) is off in both flows: nothing in eye care is quoted from photos.
Flow A's own steps: A8-x01 the eye doctor's exam after Clara's pre-tests (A8-23 is the pre-test record), A8-x04 and A8-x05 the contact lens fit and the trial pair, A8-x02 and A8-x03 dilating drops (only the eye doctor decides; a ride home is in the reminder), A8-x06 the glasses prescription handed over right after the exam, A8-x07 and A8-x08 the glasses order at the desk, A10-x01 the pick-up and fitting after Clara's READY (A10-22, Mon Nov 2; pick-up Tue Nov 3). The contact lens follow-up is booked at checkout (A10-07, Sat Oct 31).
Flow B's own steps: B8-x01 splits the visit by what was booked (money branches: an eye exam on list+none, new glasses on a deposit, an eye problem priced at the visit). The exam branch has Marcus's exam, drops (the nurse is told; no ride needed), the prescription, and the glasses order; the delivery visit is booked at DONE for Thu Nov 5 (B10-18).
Flow B is a care home, like the old dentist's: Sunrise Gardens' standing OK is on file, the nurse can meet the eye doctor, the daughter can pay. The B4-57 contract branch is off (no mobile eye care service needs a signed contract), the loaner branch (B10-07) and the storage fee (B10-27) are off, and B7-05's plan charge is off (no card saved). Kept: weather and a broken van for a visit in the eye care van.
Off in flow A: the video branch of A4-01 (an eye exam needs the office's equipment), A7-02's plan charge, day-before hold and weather branches (no card, no hold, indoor work), A10-06's rented items, and A10-30's storage fee (paid orders are kept with no fee). The pilot's plug-in-split decisions stay (splitsKept A4-43, A7-61, A8-02; B8-71, B8-72).
Texts: customer texts carry only the business, the date, the time and the place (in flow B also the eye doctor's or optician's name, for the door check): never the visit type, the plan, a result or a prescription. Owner and staff texts use initials only and carry the visit type behind a link (a last pass in the build turns every full name in an owner or staff text into initials). Safety and the danger words stay in the patient's own words.
Danger words (pf.safety): sudden vision loss, flashes, a curtain over the vision, a chemical splash or something stuck in the eye, or an eye hit hard: the emergency room or 911, no booking. A red or sore eye goes on to the eye problem visit after one safety question about flashes (B3-18). Crisis words still get 988.
Clocks: every listed path runs forward in sections 3 to 10 (checked by a script): A7-55 moved to Fri Oct 23, A8-36 got its time, B10-25 runs after the rating, and B10-18 has no time of its own. Glasses are ready days later: Mon Nov 2 at the office, Thu Nov 5 at the care home.
Renames: the pilot's pairs were kept on the master's words, with their right sides turned to eye care; pairs for the article ('a barbershop' to 'an eye care office') go right before their words; the optometrist's own sentence pairs go first (pairs.js), and some pilot pairs got new right sides by their left side (setpairs). Kept words: none.
Gaps: an order picked up when it's ready (A10-06), a paper handed over at the visit before any sale (A8-52), and the service picking which plan is checked (A4-53).
Review (Oct 23): S11-92 now says eye care pays no $2; the stand-in for an eye exam is Sam, never Leo (B7-20); no health detail in A8-38's texts; the office's texts and buttons name no eye doctor (A7-17); the glasses come back with Leo (B8-x07, B10-18), as the story says; the main path's texts say the office bills the plan (B4-15, B4-29, B5-03, B7-01); low vision aids take nothing before, as sign-up sets them (S1-38, B8-28, pf.services); an eye problem visit is billed the company's own way, private pay too (S1-16); pay over time is off (B9-19); S12-26's double charge is a real $40 glasses deposit; frames come only after the prescription (A8-x03).
